topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, the cancer lecture series, and the session's learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Fundamentals of Cancer Evolution and Mutational Drivers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the core concept of cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease driven by somatic mutations from intrinsic and extrinsic sources.

topics.label: Environmental Carcinogens, Public Perception, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine environmental exposures, the debate over random chance versus lifestyle factors, and geographic variations in cancer incidence.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how infectious agents and regional co-factors drive oncogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Molecular Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the biochemical pathways through which radiation, dietary toxins, and xenobiotically metabolized chemicals cause DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Host Susceptibility, and Mechanism Summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how non-mutagenic promoters, tissue inflammation, and host proliferative states enable cancer outgrowth before summarizing carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting Carcinogenicity and Mutational Signatures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to determine whether agents cause cancer.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by reflecting on everyday risk-benefit decisions and summarizing the complexity of identifying carcinogens.
